title: In 40 moving C. elegans, behaviour-locked activity held 56% of reliable pair-specific co-activity and wiring at most 5% of the rest; in 22 zebrafish larvae swim and flash terms held 24-36%
abstract: Question: earlier campaign work found that pair-specific functional connectivity (FC, after node effects and distance) is very reliable, that wiring explains only 3-11% of it, and that rank-3 node factors hold most of it. What are these factors? Method: in each animal we fitted every neuron or region with a cross-validated ridge model of lagged behaviour (worm: velocity, reversal, head angle, angular velocity, pumping, curvature, body shape; zebrafish: swim and dark-flash terms). This splits each pair covariance into behaviour-explained, residual and cross parts. Split-half covariances across animals measured the share of the reliable pair-specific map in each part; a control used time-shifted behaviour. Three-part splits tested tuning maps and node factors from other animals. Data: 40 off-food worms (Atanas 2023; 119 neurons), 8 on-food worms (Dag 2023), 22 larval zebrafish (Legare 2025; 65 regions). Results: in worms, 56% (95% CI 52-60%) of the reliable pair-specific covariance was behaviour-locked (shifted control 2%) and 27% survived as reliable residual covariance; on food, 72% (58-85%). In zebrafish, 36% (26-46%) with flashes and 24% (17-31%) in spontaneous activity. A map made only from other animals' tuning coefficients removed 55% of the reliable worm map, equal to a rank-1 factor. The worm factors were the forward-reversal axis (r = 0.72 with reversal tuning), a slow session drift (r = 0.61 with time) and pumping (r = 0.38). Removing behaviour did not unmask wiring: wiring explained 2.5% before and 2.8-5.4% after (time-shifted controls 3.0-3.1%). In the residual, a type-by-transmitter block model explained 13.5% (null 2.0%; on food 12.3%). Limitations: behaviour-locked is not behaviour-caused; linear model with measured variables only; the drift factor can be state or trace processing; connectome and activity from different animals; identity analysis and variants were post hoc; no fly time series.
